claims.text: The improved high-temperature mechanical behavior of refractory high-entropy alloys is governed by the in situ formation of a nanoscale ordered phase.
The improved high-temperature thermoelastic behavior of refractory high-entropy alloys is governed by the in situ formation of a nanoscale ordered phase.
As-cast refractory high-entropy alloys exist as homogeneous disordered solid solutions.
A controlled high-temperature thermal treatment can induce nanoscale ordering without changing the alloy's overall composition.
The thermal treatment forms nanoscale ordered precipitates.
Nanoscale ordered precipitates impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength.
Nanoscale ordered precipitates modify the lattice response to temperature.
Modification of the lattice response by ordered precipitates changes the coefficient of thermal expansion.
Thermally treated samples will have greater yield strength than as-cast samples.
Thermally treated samples will have a higher elastic modulus than as-cast samples.
Thermally treated samples will have a different thermal expansion coefficient from as-cast samples.
Grain-boundary strengthening or residual-stress effects may contribute to the observed mechanical and thermoelastic changes.
